description: GeoFabrics is a Python package for preparing hydrologically conditioned elevation rasters and roughness maps. Its repository describes routines that combine LiDAR points, vector information such as catchments and infrastructure, and a reference elevation raster. The project publishes source code, examples, tests, installation instructions, a wiki and generated API documentation. GitHub identifies a public GPL-3.0 repository, and the package is available through PyPI and conda-forge at no listed price. A flood modeller could use it to turn terrain and mapped waterway inputs into a consistent surface before running a hydraulic simulation. The New Zealand 8 m flood-input dataset described in Geoscience Data Journal names GeoFabrics as part of its production route. The software is a preparation tool, not itself a hydraulic solver or a validated flood forecast. Output quality depends on LiDAR coverage, mapped culverts, bathymetry and the conditioning choices. The repository was inspected but no package was installed or run. The tool can generate inputs akin to the separate New Zealand Zenodo release recorded in this G4 review.
